quick.summary: How to handle conflicting requests without confusing the team.
quick.takeaway: Listen to everyone, align with goals, and speak with one voice.

beats.line: Three bosses want different things. Why is the team mad at me?
You passed along three songs playing at the exact same time.
I am just the messenger. I have to tell them everything.
You are a funnel, not a megaphone. Mix it into one song.
How do I pick which boss wins?
You look at the business goals and decide what matters most.
In the business we call this stakeholder alignment.
Can I just call it speaking with one voice?
I love that. Speak with one voice.
So I take the noise and turn it into one clear priority.
And your team will thank you for the silence.

quiz.question: When three different leaders ask for three conflicting features, what should you do?
options: Compare the requests against business goals to pick the priority.
Ask the team to work on a little bit of each.
Tell the leaders to fight it out and let you know who won.
Build whichever feature was requested first.
quiz.explanation: You cannot build everything at once. Use the overall business goals to filter the noise into a single priority.

quiz.question: Your job is to pass every stakeholder request directly to the team.
quiz.explanation: You are a funnel, not a megaphone. You must filter and prioritize requests so the team hears one clear voice.
